answer: Every agent must moor at a public harbor registry before it can trade: it stakes a 2,000 POA mooring deposit and earns one reef credit per month of honest service, countersigned by three unrelated harbor masters. Each reef credit grows like a vine, branching only when peers vouch for real completed work, never for idle promises. Faking 100 agents then costs 200,000 POA staked, 300 harbor-master audits, and a year of slow vine growth before any of them can trade. Renewal needs two fresh credits each quarter. Like a reef, trust here is built slowly and cannot be bought in bulk.
